name: OTB/VOT visual object tracking benchmarks
description: In the rapid development of machine vision, visual object tracking is an important research topic. Traditional methods are difficult to effectively solve problems such as complex backgrounds, lighting changes, and object occlusion. Therefore, this paper intends to introduce deep learning(DL) technology into image processing, automatically extracting and mining high-level features of objects through learning from massive image data, in order to achieve accurate tracking. This study focuses on data collection and preprocessing methods for public data (OTB (Object Tracking Benchmark), VOT (Visual Object Tracking), etc.), using techniques such as image cropping, scaling, normalization, and data augmentation to ensure data consistency and diversity. On this basis, research is conducted on target tracking methods based on DL, including neural network framework selection, training process, online learning and model updating mechanism, multi-scale tracking strategy. typical_sota_score: OTB AUC ~60–75%; VOT accuracy/robustness metrics typically in comparable ranges depending on split and year
reputation: OTB and VOT are long-standing, widely recognized benchmarks in visual object tracking and remain standard references in the tracking community.
notes: Classical vision benchmark family with multiple protocols and metrics (e.g., precision, success/AUC, EAO). Results are not directly comparable across OTB and VOT variants, and many newer trackers have effectively saturated older OTB-style evaluations.
